question.text: Calc: 'Brahmaputra Credit Fund', a Category II AIF, has target commitments of INR 600 crore. The Sponsor wishes to minimize GP capital lock-in while remaining compliant. What is the minimum mandatory Sponsor/Manager continuing interest required?

answer.text: INR 5 crore (lower of 2.5% = INR 15 cr and INR 5 cr cap)
INR 30 crore (5% of 600 cr, as the fund intends to take leverage)

explanation.text: The Logic: For a Category I or II AIF, the Sponsor/Manager continuing interest is not less than 2.5% of the corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower. For a corpus of INR 600 crore, 2.5% works out to INR 15 crore; the lower of INR 15 crore and the INR 5 crore cap is INR 5 crore. The "whichever is lower" cap intentionally limits the absolute GP commitment as the corpus scales up. The Trap: Option A applies the 2.5% rate but ignores the INR 5 crore cap. Option C uses a 10% rate that does not feature in the Cat I/II continuing-interest rule. Option D applies the Cat III rate (5%) and then layers on a non-existent leverage adjustment, both of which are unsupported. Note: For Cat I/II, anchor on "2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower"; for Cat III, the equivalent rule is "5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is lower" with the same lower-of mechanic.
